01

Brand Foundation

Before a color or a font, there's a reason we exist. Everything visual is downstream of this. If a design ever feels off, it's usually because it drifted from one of these ideas.

Mission

oSTEM @ OU empowers LGBTQ+ students in science, technology, engineering, and math to thrive — personally, academically, and professionally — and builds a community where every Sooner in STEM can bring their whole self to the lab, the lecture hall, and the career fair.

Vision

A University of Oklahoma where being queer in STEM isn't something you navigate around — it's a source of connection, confidence, and creative advantage. Where no one has to choose between their identity and their field.

Positioning — the one sentence that governs everything

For LGBTQ+ students and allies in STEM at OU, oSTEM is the professional community that turns isolation into belonging and identity into an advantage — because the best science happens when no one has to hide.

What we value

Belonging

Chosen family first. Everyone gets a seat before they earn one.

Excellence

Queer joy and STEM rigor are not a trade-off. We do both, well.

Visibility

Representation is data. We make queer scientists impossible to overlook.

Curiosity

We ask, we build, we tinker — with our work and with each other's stories.

Care

Safety, consent, and looking out for one another are non-negotiable.

Joy

This is allowed to be fun. Delight is a feature, not a distraction.

Brand personality

If oSTEM @ OU walked into a room, it would be the person who is warm enough to make you feel instantly welcome, confident enough to never apologize for existing, curious enough to ask what you're working on, rigorous enough to actually help you fix it — and joyful enough that you'd want to come back next week.

WarmConfidentCuriousRigorousJoyful

The idea that ties the whole brand together

Every petal is a discipline. Every color is a person. The flower only works because all six are there — and its reddest petal is already the color of Oklahoma.

02

Voice & Tone

People forget layouts. They remember how you made them feel. Our words do more heavy lifting than any gradient. Here's how we sound — and, just as important, how we stay safe and credible while sounding like ourselves.

Four voice principles

1  Human before institutional

Write like a real person who is genuinely glad you showed up — not like a policy. "Pull up a chair," not "All students are welcome to attend."

2  Confident, never defensive

We don't justify our existence or ask permission to take up space. We simply invite people in. Assume you belong; so will they.

3  Witty, never at anyone's expense

Humor that includes, never punches. A little chaos in a caption is on-brand; irony that could wound is not.

4  Precise when it counts

Dates, rooms, deadlines, and professional comms are crisp and correct. Rigor is how a queer org earns the room. Sloppiness is never cute.

Read the room: tone shifts by context

ContextDial it toSounds like
Instagram caption / storyPlayful & warm"okay but who's actually surviving thermodynamics this week 😩 come decompress with us thursday."
Event announcementClear & energetic"Queer Coffee & Code — Thu 6 PM, Devon Energy Hall 120. Free coffee, real study help, zero pressure."
Faculty / recruiter emailPolished & professional"Thank you for supporting oSTEM @ OU. Here's a one-page overview of our members and how a partnership could work."
Sensitive / hard momentsCalm & steady"We see you, and we're here. If today is heavy, our door — and our DMs — are open."

Inclusive language — the essentials

Reach forRetireWhy
y'all, folks, everyoneyou guysGendered defaults leave people out; "y'all" is also very Oklahoma.
pronounspreferred pronounsThey aren't a preference. They're just someone's pronouns.
orientationsexual preference"Preference" implies a choice; it also reads as dated.
LGBTQ+ / queer (reclaimed, in-community)alphabet soup, "lifestyle"Match oSTEM National's usage; "queer" is our warm in-group word.
partnerboyfriend/girlfriend (assumed)Never assume the gender of someone's person.
chosen namereal name / preferred nameTheir chosen name is their real name.
Reading the state we're in — safety & credibility in Oklahoma

We operate at a public university in a conservative state. That doesn't mean shrinking — it means being smart, so we stay standing. Three habits protect our people and our reputation at once:

1. Lead with community & career. oSTEM is, truthfully, a professional-development and belonging organization. That framing is both accurate and durable — it protects funding, faculty support, and standing. Let the work be the armor.

2. Consent is the default for every face. Offer a visible opt-out at events (a lanyard color, a "no-photo" sticker). Never tag or name a member without a yes. One careless repost can out someone to family or an employer.

3. Guard the vulnerable specifics. Promote sensitive gatherings via RSVP or DM rather than broadcasting every detail publicly. Widen the tent with "students and allies" — it's true, it's welcoming, and it's protective.

Messaging pillars — what we actually talk about

Belonging & chosen family Professional growth Queer excellence & visibility Joy & culture

Roughly every post, story, and poster should ladder up to one of these four. If it doesn't, ask whether it's ours to say.

03

The Logo System

Two marks, one family. The flower is our heart — hand-painted, six petals radiating from a golden core, blossoming outward. The full lockup ties us to the national org and to OU. Use the flower to be felt; use the lockup to be official.

The flower mark

Our signature. Profile pictures, stickers, story icons, merch, watermarks. Instantly ours even with no words attached — that's the goal.

The full lockup

Flower + oSTEM wordmark + the Progress color bar + "University of Oklahoma." The formal signature for flyers, letterheads, banners, slide decks, and anything official.

Clear space & minimum size

Give the mark room to breathe. Keep clear space on all sides equal to the height of the flower's golden center. Nothing — text, edges, other logos — enters that zone.

Minimum sizes

So it never turns to mud:

Flower mark — never below 32 px on screen / 0.4 in in print.

Full lockup — never below 140 px wide / 1.2 in, so "University of Oklahoma" stays legible.

Backgrounds

Best on cream, white, or a clean crimson field. On busy photos, place the mark on a solid crimson or cream chip first. Keep strong contrast, always.

Protect the mark — the don'ts

Don'tRecolor or reorder the petals. The six colors are fixed — they're people, not decoration.
Don'tRotate, skew, squish, or add drop-shadows, glows, or outlines to the flower.
Don'tRebuild the wordmark in a different font or respace it. Use the supplied files only.
Don'tPlace the mark on a low-contrast or clashing color that fights the petals.
Don'tCrowd it with text or other logos inside the clear-space zone.
DoScale proportionally, keep it crisp, and when unsure — more space, not less.
04

Color — The Spectrum

Our palette has two jobs. Crimson & Cream say University of Oklahoma — our home, our credibility, our gravitas. The Spectrum — the six petals plus the golden heart — says us. Crimson holds the frame; the rainbow fills it in.

The happy accident that became our strategy: the flower's top petal samples at #971F29 and its core at #8B1A24 — a breath away from OU Crimson. The university was inside the bloom the whole time. So we never fight crimson against the rainbow; we let the rainbow grow out of it.

How to mix them — the 60 / 30 / 10 rule

60% — Cream / Crimson base 30% — Crimson structure 10% — Spectrum accent

Let cream and crimson do most of the work — that restraint is what makes us feel timeless rather than busy. Bring in a spectrum color (or the full rainbow) as the moment: a headline underline, a highlighted word, a single petal, the color bar. When you want maximum pride energy (Pride Month, big socials), invert briefly to a full-rainbow hero — then return to calm. Don't tint text in six colors at once outside of celebration pieces.

Accessibility is part of belonging

Body text: Ink on Cream, or Cream on Crimson — both clear WCAG AA. Never put Sunlight (#EBC038) or Gold (#E5AF30) text on white — pair those on Ink or Crimson instead. Keep body type at 4.5:1 contrast minimum, and always write image alt text and caption your videos. If someone can't read it, we didn't say it.

05

Typography

Two typefaces. That's the discipline. One for impact, one for reading — both free, both in Canva and Google Fonts, both a little warm and very modern. Restraint here is what reads as "designed."

Display & Headlines — Poppins
Bring your whole self.

Geometric, optimistic, and a cousin of the rounded letters in our own oSTEM wordmark. Use SemiBold (600) and Bold (700) for headlines, event titles, and big statements. Tight letter-spacing on large sizes.

Body & UI — Inter
Clarity is kindness. Inter keeps captions, details, schedules, and long copy effortlessly readable at any size — on a phone screen at a bus stop or a poster across a hallway.

Regular (400) and Medium (500) for body; SemiBold (600) for labels and eyebrows in ALL CAPS with wide tracking.

Editorial accent (use sparingly) — Fraunces Italic
“The best science happens when no one has to hide.”

One optional flourish, for pull-quotes and the occasional tagline. It adds soul and a touch of the academic. A little goes a long way — never set body text or a whole poster in it.

The type scale

RoleFont / weightFeel
Hero / poster titlePoppins Bold 700Big, tight, unmissable
Section headingPoppins SemiBold 600Structured, calm
Eyebrow / labelInter SemiBold 600, UPPERCASE, +trackingQuiet signpost
BodyInter Regular / MediumReadable, human
Pull-quote (rare)Fraunces ItalicSoulful, editorial
DoPair Poppins headline + Inter body. Keep generous line-height. Left-align long copy. Use one accent color per layout.
Don'tMix in a third random font, stretch or condense type, center long paragraphs, or set body copy in Fraunces.
06

Imagery & Motif

Our look is warm, real, and a little hand-made — never stock-photo sterile. The flower is the connective tissue; petals are our punctuation.

Photography

Real members, real moments — candid over posed, natural light, genuine laughter. Warm color grade that leans into cream and crimson. Show hands building, screens glowing, whiteboards mid-thought, people mid-conversation. Every face has consented. Diversity is the default, not a checkbox.

The flower as motif

Beyond the logo, the flower is a texture we reuse: a single petal as a bullet or tag, the six colors as a divider bar, an oversized petal bleeding off a poster edge, the bloom watermarked at low opacity behind a quote. Recognizable in a glance, never cluttered.

Graphic language

Rounded corners (12–16px). Generous whitespace. Soft crimson shadows, never hard black. The Progress color bar as a recurring device. One idea per graphic. When a layout feels busy, remove — don't add. Our minimalism is deliberate: it's how a student org reads as trustworthy.

Instagram is our front door. Most students will meet us here before they ever walk into a room. So the grid isn't a scrapbook — it's the first impression, run consistently.

The caption formula — Hook · Heart · Handoff

Hook — one scroll-stopping line. A question, a feeling, a joke.
Heart — two or three lines of the actual value or story.
Handoff — a clear next step: when, where, and what to do.

okay but who's actually surviving thermodynamics this week? 😩
Come decompress with us Thursday — free coffee, real study help from people who've been there, and absolutely zero pressure to know what you're doing.
📍 Devon Energy Hall 120 · 6 PM Thursday · everyone & every ally welcome. Tap the link to RSVP. 🌸

Every post, every time: write image alt text, caption your Reels, put hashtags in the first comment to keep captions clean, and check color contrast on text-over-image.

Hashtags

#oSTEMatOU#QueerInSTEM#LGBTQinSTEM#oSTEM#OUSooners#BoomerSooner

Lead with the core set above, then add 3–5 rotating tags per post (event, topic, or campaign). Always CamelCase multi-word tags (#QueerInSTEM, not #queerinstem) — screen readers depend on it.

Stories & Highlights

Run Stories for the day-to-day (event countdowns, behind-the-scenes, reposts, polls). Keep a clean set of Highlight covers — the flower or single petals on crimson — one per evergreen category:

AboutEventsTeamResourcesRecapsJoin

Cadence

Aim for 3–4 feed posts a week, Stories most days, and a rhythm around each event: a teaser (a week out), a day-of reminder, and a recap (within 48 hours). Consistency beats volume — a steady, on-brand grid builds trust faster than sporadic bursts.

08

Posters & Canva

Most of our posters get made in Canva, fast, often the night before. So the system has to be foolproof. Here's the anatomy — and a worked example you can literally rebuild.

oSTEM @ OU · Happening

Queer
Coffee
& Code

study together, decompress together
Thu · 6:00 PM Devon Energy Hall 120 Free coffee · real study help Everyone & every ally welcome
@ostem_ou

Why this poster works — read it like a designer

  1. Crimson field, cream type. The deep-crimson gradient background instantly says "OU" and lets one oversized flower carry all the color. High contrast = readable across a hallway.
  2. One flower, doing the pride work. A single petal-bleed off the top corner brings the full spectrum without six competing text colors. Restraint is the flex.
  3. Poppins title, tight & huge. Three short stacked words own the poster. You can read the what from 20 feet; the details reward a closer look.
  4. Fraunces italic sub-line. One soulful, human line under the title — the single editorial flourish, exactly where it earns its place.
  5. Details in a clean Inter stack. When · where · what · who, in that order, scannable in a second. "Every ally welcome" widens the tent and quietly protects us.
  6. QR + handle + color bar as the footer. A frictionless next step, our name, and the Progress bar as a signature — the same device from the logo, tying poster back to brand.
Canva setup

Size 1080×1350 (feed) or 1080×1920 (story/print A-frame). Load brand colors into Brand Kit so the palette is one click. Upload the flower PNG + logo lockup once. Set Poppins + Inter as the two text styles. Save this as a reusable template — next officer just swaps the words.

Poster checklist before it goes out

Check
✓Logo or flower present, with clear space respected
✓Only Poppins + Inter (+ maybe one Fraunces line)
✓Crimson/cream base, one spectrum accent (or a full-rainbow moment on purpose)
✓When · Where · What · Who — all four answerable in 3 seconds
✓A next step: QR, @handle, or RSVP link
✓Text passes contrast; nothing important within 0.25in of the edge
09

Applications

The same small kit, everywhere we appear. Consistency across surfaces is what turns a logo into a brand people trust.

Profile picture

Flower centered on a solid OU Crimson circle. Identical across Instagram, Discord, LinkedIn, GroupMe. Never the full lockup — too small to read.

Highlight covers

Flower or single petals on crimson, one per evergreen category. Quiet, uniform, unmistakably ours.

Email signature

Small lockup + name, role, pronouns, and a single crimson line. Poppins name, Inter details.

Name badges

Big first name (Poppins), pronouns beneath, flower in the corner, spectrum bar along the bottom. Blank pronoun line = a choice, always.

T-shirts & merch

Oversized flower on cream or crimson; small wordmark. One color story per garment. Let the bloom be the hero.

Tabling banner

Crimson field, giant flower, three words of value, @handle + QR. Readable from across the union in one glance.

Slides & Zoom

Cream slides, crimson headers, flower top-corner, spectrum divider. A crimson virtual background with a small flower for panels.

Stickers

Die-cut flower. The single most powerful piece of merch we own — free brand ambassadors on every laptop.

Faculty one-pager

Polished, professional lockup up top; community & career framing; clean Inter body. This is our credibility document.

10

Keeping the Legacy

Officers graduate; the brand shouldn't. This is how oSTEM @ OU still looks like oSTEM @ OU in five years — no matter who's holding the phone.

The Brand Kit lives in one place

A shared drive folder + a Canva Team, holding: logo files (flower + lockup, PNG/SVG), this guide, the color palette, the two fonts, and every reusable template. One link in the officer handbook. If it's not in the kit, it isn't official.

One person owns the look

A Marketing/Branding lead approves anything public-facing before it posts. Not to gatekeep — to keep the promise consistent. They onboard the next lead with this doc.

New-officer onboarding — 15 minutes

Read this guide. Join the Canva Team. Save the flower + lockup. Set Poppins + Inter. Post one on-brand test graphic and get a thumbs-up. Done — you're fluent.

The 10-second test

Cover the logo. Could a stranger still tell this is oSTEM @ OU — from the crimson, the cream, the flower, the type, the warmth of the words? If yes, ship it. If no, it's not ours yet.

The consistency checklist

✓OU Crimson & Cream carry the design; the spectrum accents it
✓Poppins headlines, Inter body — nothing else
✓Flower or lockup present, clear space respected
✓Warm, confident, human words — witty, never at anyone's cost
✓Consent for every face; "students & allies" where it fits
✓Accessible: alt text, captions, contrast
✓One clear next step on anything public

Every petal, a discipline. Every color, a person.
